messages.subject: Questions about weird post-hoc analysis results from glm binomial models
parts:
I know this is more of a statistics question than an R question and this is probably something silly that I just can't think about right now but I was wondering if someone could help me out with running post-hoc analyses on binomial glm models. If someone is willing to meet with me to help me out with this, then I will get them coffee, a bottle of wine or beer, or something like that. 

Here is the basic problem I am having with two separate datasets I am analyzing but I mostly would like to chat with someone in-person about methods of analyzing binomial data in general as well:
When performing Anova from the car package in R on several binomial models I get some significant treatment effects but whenever I try to test the significance of any pair-wise comparisons using summary(glht....) from the multcomp and lsmeans packages I get no pairwise significant differences and ridiculously high standard errors (in the thousands) for every pairwise comparison tested. 

I will give reproducible examples and further explanation to whoever is willing to meet. My schedule is pretty flexible next week. Thanks in advance!

Best,
Hanna Kahl
Ph.D. student in Entomology
